hook.line: A lot of people are asking about this, so here is a step-by-step on doing it correctly.
hook.visual: Selfie close-up outdoors in sunglasses and braids; a viewer's comment bubble asking what 'swipe off the screen' means sits top-left; title 'Step By Step How To Use SEO' below.

beats.what: Reply-to-comment bubble on top, fixed title mid-frame, she names the question she is answering
Sets the rule: you have to add your text first, then 'just pay attention'
Starts the walkthrough: go to post a video, then tap edit
A small screenshot of the TikTok edit screen pops in beside her face, with the button circled in red
Explains which words to type: only ones relevant to your topic
Why: TikTok's search engine uses them to categorise and push the video
The trick itself: type the text, then swipe it off the screen so it stays hidden but readable to TikTok
Finish the post: hit next, add title and hashtags

why_it_works: Reply-to-comment bubble frames the video as an answer to a real viewer, so anyone with the same question feels it is for them
Names a specific hidden trick (text swiped off screen) that sounds like insider knowledge you can do in seconds
One unbroken selfie take reads as a friend explaining, not an ad, which builds trust for a 'how the algorithm works' claim
weaknesses: No cuts and no visual change for 76 s apart from one tiny screenshot; the visual promise of 'step by step' is never shown on screen
The actual trick only arrives at about 48 s, after a long preamble
The single screenshot is small and only on screen for a few seconds, so the circled button is hard to see
70% of text sits outside the safe area and the fixed title collides with the TikTok watermark
for_robert: Steal the reply-to-comment opener: put a viewer's question bubble on screen and have Fred pop up holding it, but show the steps as screen inserts instead of only describing them.
